chapter_theme: The second part of the woman's lament: he who was everywhere undid her maidenhood and broke her chastity, and she asks what will come of it, whether caste or sect or the sastras will have her now, and what crime she committed. From the questions the verses turn to describing him to her friend with the refrain காண் ('see!'): beyond speech and mind, the fire-light hidden in a stone, the light within a ruby, the one who made her stay still in the void past burning. She confesses that she had fallen into the void without devotion, and the part ends with the cause that is shown by a hand and not learned or heard, and the one that speech cannot reach.
structure_note: 531 to 534 complete the story of the taking; 535 to 541 are questions to the friend about caste, crime, seeing and speaking; 542 to 547 and 550 to 551 describe him in -காண் lines; 548 and 549 are near-doublets of Azhuganni 37 and 38, and 550 of Azhuganni 39; 552 and 553 confess the failure before him. Units 1 to 48 of the work come from two source files; from 555 on the text is in a single file and printed without word spacing. Seq 554 is an empty unit and is not in the chapter.

531.reading: He saw this state of mine and was everywhere; he destroyed my maidenhood, he broke my chastity.
531.nuance: The bridal cipher of the lament: கன்னி அழித்தல் and கற்பைக் குலைத்தல் are the Lord's taking of the soul, told as a seduction. What the chastity stands for is not said; the soul's fidelity to its own bonds, or its separateness, are the usual readings, and the shock of the words is deliberate. எங்கும் இருந்தான், he was everywhere, names the taker as the all-pervading.

532.reading: The breaking of my chastity, the cutting of the womb's root, the ruin of my beauty, the loss of my awareness:
532.nuance: A list of four -அமை nouns that is completed by 533. பொற்பு is grace or beauty of form; போதம், awareness, is what 515 also says he took.

533.reading: what deed will come of all this to me I do not yet know; every word he said has come true, without fail.
533.nuance: சொன்ன சொல்லெல்லாம் பலித்தது: the guru's word is tested by its coming true, which is the lament's only proof of him. வினை here may be karma or simply what happens next.

534.reading: He showed and handed over to me the place without night and day; he destroyed my shame; I stood looking at him who looked.
534.nuance: கங்குல் பகல் அற்ற இடம், the place with no night or day, is plainly timelessness; in the Siddhars' cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, so it is also the state past them. பங்கம் is defect or disgrace. பார்த்தானைப் பார்த்திருந்தேன் is a mutual gaze, which tradition hears as the initiation by look.

535.reading: Will they admit me to caste? Will I fall within the sastras? Reciting and realising, everything became just as it is.
535.nuance: The two questions are the ruined girl's and the jnani's at once: neither caste nor scripture has a place for her now. உள்ளபடி ஆச்சு, 'became as it is', is the plainest statement of the result in the work.

536.reading: What fault did I commit? Though no one saw, would not my mother and all my kin know of it in this wide world?
536.nuance: The plain sense is the girl's dread that an unseen fall will be known at home. The coded sense keeps the shape: the change in the realised one was unseen, yet shows.

537.reading: Did I eat those who killed? Did I kill those who ate? Did I forget the desire that thinks every unthinkable thing?
537.nuance: The first line is a riddle. As protest it means 'I did no crime of that kind'; as cipher it can mean she destroyed the senses that kill and killed the appetites that eat. The third question says what she actually did: she forgot desire (இச்சை), which is the only 'crime' the world sees.

538.reading: Will they admit me to caste? Will the people of the sects count me in? All my life lived in division has become matter for talk.
538.nuance: பேதித்து வாழ்ந்தது, living in difference, is her former life among caste and sect; it is now gossip (பேச்சுக்கு இடம்). The questions repeat 535 with sect in place of sastra.

539.reading: To those who see, am I not a woman? For those who do not see there is desire too. Did those who ate eat anything other than food?
539.nuance: The sense turns on who sees what. One reading: whoever looks at her sees only a woman, and even the blind feel desire, so the world will read her state as sex; and yet whatever anyone eats is only food, so the many are one thing. Another takes கண்டார் as those who have seen the truth. The verse is left as a riddle.

540.reading: What those who took took, will those who did not take take it? Have those who spoke seen? Have those who saw spoken?
540.nuance: The second line is a form of the Siddhars' maxim that the seers do not tell and the tellers have not seen. கொண்டவர் (those who took, or who were taken in marriage) carries the bridal cipher into the first line.

541.reading: Is it the gift the four ancient Vedas sing of? Does it appear and settle in the heart of servants who are truly servants?
541.nuance: Both questions may be rhetorical denials (the Vedas cannot sing it, nor does it stay in any heart), or the second may answer the first: not in the Vedas but in the servant's heart. தொண்டாய தொண்டர், servants who are servants, points to the second.

542.reading: Is it easy to recite? Is it hard for anyone to realise? He is the great one who shines everywhere without difference.
542.nuance: The first -காண் verse: from here the speaker describes him to the friend. பேதமற (without difference) answers the பேதித்து of 538.

543.reading: He is the one beyond speech and mind, in whom the mind dissolves; he is hard to look upon, the subtle one among the subtle.
543.nuance: மனோலயன் may be 'he in whom the mind dissolves' or 'he who is the dissolving of mind'. நுண்ணியரில் நுண்ணியன் is the Siddhars' சூட்சம், the subtle thing within; 556 ends the part with the same claim in Sanskrit.

544.reading: He is not contained in words; he stands beyond words; he stands like the fire-light that was within the stone.
544.nuance: கல்லுள் இருந்த கனல் ஒளி, the fire latent in a stone, is present but shows only when struck; the image returns at 591 in the fourth part of the work.

545.reading: He told me to stay melting in the void beyond heat. Is it a letter on the leaf, or a slip of the hand of the one who wrote it?
545.nuance: சூடு இறந்த பாழ், the void past burning, is the state after all the burning of the first part; கசிந்திருக்க, to stay oozing or melting, is tenderness rather than heat. The second line asks whether her fate was written (ஏட்டில் எழுத்து, the script of destiny) or is an error of the writer, Brahma; the two lines may not belong together.

546.reading: He made me stay still; I do not know the formula. Mother! saying 'this is the meaning', he swallowed me whole.
546.nuance: சும்மா இரு, 'just be', is the Tamil Siddhars' central teaching, and the speaker says she was made to do it without knowing the சூத்திரம், the rule behind it. விழுங்கினண்டி is read as he swallowed (விழுங்கினான் + அடி), the absorption image that 580 and 581 develop; 'I swallowed it whole' is also possible.

547.reading: Everywhere I looked I saw as the Supreme; I no longer know any doctrine whose strung order has collapsed.
547.nuance: கோத்த நிலை குலைந்த கொள்கை is a position whose threading has come apart; once all is seen as பரம், there is no tenet to hold. 568 answers with the Lord who takes the strung state for those who string.

548.reading: Without bathing the image and plucking flowers to adorn it, my heart became a bare void; I do not see the state in which I stood.
548.nuance: The rites of worship are not refuted but simply not done, and what is left is வெறும் பாழ், an emptiness the speaker cannot even locate. The Azhuganni doublet (37) is the same couplet with its refrain.

549.reading: Though I had sung and studied, without adorning many flowers, without running about, I lost my form.
549.nuance: ஓடித் திரியாமல், not running about, is the pilgrim's running to shrines; உருக்கெட்டு is plainly 'I was ruined' and in the cipher 'I lost form'. Azhuganni 38 is the doublet.

550.reading: He stayed mingled in me like the light within a ruby; he is the greatness that the devotees who cherish and worship him do not speak of.
550.nuance: மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி, the light in a gem, is indwelling without mixture, and 563 repeats it. பேசாப் பெருமை is a greatness not spoken, by those who know it; the silence of 540 again. Azhuganni 39 is the doublet.

551.reading: From that day to this, through the time when I knew nothing, he was always the common one, free of affliction.
551.nuance: பொது, common or impartial, is Siva's name as the one who belongs to all; நிராமயன் is the one without disease. The point is that her ignorance changed nothing in him.

552.reading: Through the mind's disturbance I did not see the one who is pure consciousness, and with my understanding confused I went in by the way of the senses.
552.nuance: சித்த விகாரம் recalls the விகாரம் the tattvas breed at 509. சின்மயன் is the Vedantic name for the Lord as consciousness; பொறிவழி, the senses' road, is the way she went instead.

553.reading: Not knowing devotion I fell headlong into the void, and stayed there in agreement, as if it were a fitting sleep.
553.nuance: The void here is a fall, not the goal of 545 and 548: without devotion the emptiness is a sleep (நித்திரை) mistaken for the state. The line is a self-question (இருந்தேண்டி?) and its grammar, ஒத்தவிட ... ஒத்தும், is awkward; the reading of 'fitting sleep' is a guess.

555.reading: Not learning, not hearing: see, the cause that points by hand; it is without limit or measure, filled everywhere.
555.nuance: கைகாட்டும் காரணம், the cause shown by a hand, is the silent teaching by gesture that tradition gives to Dakshinamurti and to the guru's hand-sign; learning and hearing are set against it. The unit is printed without word spaces.

556.reading: He came to dwell in what speech cannot reach; he is without pollution; he is the knowledge of knowledge.
556.nuance: வாசாமகோசரம் is the Sanskrit term for what lies outside the range of speech, used by Tirumular too. ஆசூசம் இல்லான், without ritual pollution, closes a part that began with a maidenhood destroyed: no impurity attaches to him or to what he did.

links.note: Tirumular says those who have set Nandi in love by knowledge have no caste, no stain and no qualities to take on; Pattinathar's speaker, having realised, asks whether caste or the sastras will have her, and the answer the Tirumanthiram gives is that the question no longer applies.
Pambatti says those who have seen never tell and those who tell have never seen; Pattinathar asks the same as a double question, have the tellers seen, have the seers told.

The Agappei tells the inner demon to just stay still and says it has told the formula (சூத்திரம்); Pattinathar's speaker was made to stay still and says she does not know the formula. Both make சும்மா இருத்தல் the teaching, and differ on whether its rule can be stated.
Azhuganni 37 is the same couplet with its ஆத்தாடி refrain: no bathing, no flowers, the heart a bare void.

Tirumular says that those who recite, worship and gather flowers without love have minds like a stone in a mossy pond; Pattinathar's speaker drops the flowers and bathing altogether and finds her heart an empty void, which she cannot yet read as gain or loss.

Tirumular's Being stays mingled within like light in a gem and is farther than far if put into words; Pattinathar's Lord stays mingled like the light within a ruby and is the greatness his devotees do not speak of. Same image, same conclusion about speech.

Both warn that a void can be mistaken for the goal: Tirumular says the foolish call the wordless void in which turiya subsides the Supreme; Pattinathar confesses she fell into the void without devotion and took it for a fitting sleep.

The Kural says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not returning, so that learning is the way to the real; Pattinathar says the cause is not learning and not hearing but what is shown by a hand. The conflict holds on the reading of கற்று as learning the true texts, which is how Parimelazhagar takes it; if the Kural means only 'having learned to see', the two agree.

Both use the same Sanskrit term: Tirumular's Nandi is வாசாமகோசரம், beyond speech and mind, where conduct, love and the Veda end; Pattinathar's Lord took his seat in வாசாமகோசரம் and is the knowledge of knowledge.

source_issues: Seq 554 (siddhar:arutpulambal-2:0276_01-49) has no text in the corpus; the unit is empty and the chapter runs 553 to 555. The work's numbering jumps from the two-source units 1 to 48 to single-source units 49 to 76.
555 and 556 (and all of 557 to 581) are printed without word spacing, from the single source pmuni0276_01; the second source pmuni0083 ends at unit 48.
The section label 'மகடூ முன்னிலையாக உள்ளது' on 555 onward is the source's note that the verses are in the feminine second person, not a heading of the poet's.
